transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… yeah, hi. I’m here because I keep hearing this man’s voice, and it’s gotten to where I can’t just ignore it or tell myself it’s nothing.

It happens at work a lot — I’m a mechanic, so I’m in the garage all day — and I’ll hear it coming through the vents, like the air vents in the shop, but not muffled like someone far away. It’s clear, like there’s a man standing right next to me talking into my ear. And sometimes it’s when I’m under the hood of a car, like the voice is coming from inside the engine bay or underneath something, even when nobody is there.

He says things like I shouldn’t trust my husband, or he’ll tell me not to touch certain cars. And I know that sounds… I know how it sounds. But in the moment it feels so real, like I can hear the direction it’s coming from and everything. It’s been scaring me, and it’s messing with me at work because I’ll hesitate before doing something I’ve done a thousand times. That’s really what brought me in.
Did this start while you were using alcohol or drugs?

I don’t… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’m not sitting here thinking, like, “Oh yeah, it was because of something I took,” if that’s what you mean. I haven’t connected it to that in my head.

I guess I’d have to think about it more, because the way it started didn’t feel like some one-night thing where I used something and then heard something right after. It felt more like it started creeping into regular life, if that makes sense. Like at work, during a normal day, doing normal stuff. So… I’m not sure. I don’t think I can point to alcohol or drugs as the start of it.
When you hear the voice, do you also feel confused or not fully aware of what’s going on around you?

I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think I black out or anything like that, if that’s what you mean. I’m usually still aware I’m at work, I know what I’m doing, I can see the car in front of me and hear the normal shop noises too.

But it does kind of… pull me out of the moment, I guess. Like my attention snaps to the voice because it feels so close and specific, and then I’m standing there trying to figure out if someone actually said something or if it came from the vent or from under the hood. So I can get distracted and rattled, and maybe I look confused from the outside, but I don’t think I’m totally unaware of what’s going on around me.

It’s more like everything else is still there, but the voice becomes the thing I’m focused on.
Do you believe someone is actually using the vents or the cars to speak to you on purpose?

I mean… yes. I know how that sounds, I really do. If someone said it to me a few years ago, I’d probably think it was far-fetched too. But it doesn’t feel like just a random voice or just me mishearing something.

It feels intentional. Like there’s a setup around it. Not just the vents, but the stuff in the shop — the EV chargers especially, and the security cameras. I’m pretty convinced my husband and the shop owner have been using them somehow to track what I’m doing. Like when I’m near certain bays, or when I’m working on certain cars, it’s like they already know where I am and what I’m touching.

And they’ll show me footage and say, “Look, there’s nothing there,” or they’ll act like I’m making connections that don’t exist, but that doesn’t really settle it for me. Because footage can miss things, or they can choose what to show me, or the tracking isn’t something you’d just see on a regular camera anyway. So… yeah, I think someone is doing it on purpose. I don’t really know exactly how every part works, but I don’t think it’s nothing.
How long have you been hearing this voice?

It’s been… about ten months now, I think. Not like I can point to the exact day and circle it on a calendar, but around that. Close to a year, but not quite.

At first I kept thinking maybe it was just something in the shop, like a sound carrying weird or somebody talking where I couldn’t see them, so I didn’t really mark it as “this is the start.” But looking back, it’s been going on for about ten months — the voice, and then the feeling that there’s tracking tied into it too. It hasn’t just been a couple weeks or anything. It’s been long enough that I’ve had time to keep noticing the pattern.
Over the past ten months, have you become much less interested in being around other people than you used to be?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it because it makes me sound like I’m just being rude or lazy, but there are stretches where I just don’t want to be around anybody.

Like, I’ll see people calling or texting and I just… don’t call them back. Not because I hate them or anything, I just can’t make myself pick up the phone and do the whole conversation. And church stuff used to be a big thing for me — I used to help with the potlucks, like actually be involved, set things up, make sure people had what they needed. Lately I’ll just skip it. I’ll tell myself I’m tired, or I’ll go next time, but then next time comes and I still don’t go.

And at work it happens too, kind of. I’ll be in the bay and instead of getting moving like I normally would, I’ll just be standing there looking at the tools or the bench, and it’s like I know I should care, I know I should start the next thing, but there’s this blank feeling. Like I can’t get interested in any of it.

So, yeah, I’ve pulled back from people. More than I used to. It’s not every single second, but there are definitely stretches where I just stay in the house or keep to myself and everything feels like too much effort.
Have you used methamphetamine or cocaine during the time you’ve been hearing the voice?

I’m… not totally sure how you want me to answer that. Like, do you mean any amount at all, even once, or do you mean regularly using it around the time the voice started?

I get why you’re asking, because people always jump to “it must be drugs” when someone says they’re hearing something, but I don’t really have a neat answer ready in my head for that. If you mean something specific by “used,” maybe you can tell me exactly what counts, and I can try to answer it more clearly.
During these past ten months, have you used methamphetamine?

I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I hear you asking specifically methamphetamine, and I’m not trying to dodge it, I just… I’m not sure what counts in the way you’re asking.

Like, I don’t have a clear “yes, this was happening every week” kind of answer sitting in my head. If you mean, was I regularly using meth during this whole ten months, I don’t think that’s how I’d describe it. But if you mean any exposure, any time, even if it was around people or something happened once, then I’d have to think harder because my memory around all of it isn’t organized neatly.

I know that probably sounds evasive. I’m sorry. I just don’t want to say yes or no and then have it be the wrong kind of answer.
Have the voice and the feeling of being tracked ever started or gotten worse after you stopped drinking alcohol?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern like that.

I mean, I understand what you’re asking — like whether after I stop drinking, then the voice or that tracked feeling kicks up — but I don’t have it mapped out in my head that neatly. When things get bad, I’m usually already stressed and not sleeping right or just trying to get through the day, so I don’t always stop and think, “Okay, did this happen after alcohol or before alcohol?”

So… I can’t honestly say yes to that. I don’t remember sitting there thinking, “Oh, I stopped drinking and now this is worse.” It doesn’t stand out to me that way. If you need me to, I can try to think through specific times, but just answering right now, I don’t know that I’ve noticed that connection.
During these ten months, have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… yes, that did happen. Not just like one bad night of sleep, either. There were stretches where for weeks at a time I’d only sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I’d wake up before dawn already wide awake, like my head was already at the garage before my body was even up.

It didn’t feel like normal insomnia, where you’re exhausted and miserable and just can’t sleep. It was more like… sleeping felt like a waste of time. Like if I stayed in bed, I was losing hours I could be using. I’d be thinking about work, tools, cars, parts, things I wanted to fix or organize, and my mind would already be running before the sun was up.

And at the time I wouldn’t always think, “This is unusual.” I’d kind of tell myself I was just being productive or that I had momentum. But looking back, yeah, it was definitely much less sleep than usual, and I still felt like I had energy to keep going.
When you were sleeping only two or three hours a night, were you hearing the voice then?

Yes. Yeah, that was happening then too.

When I was in those stretches where I was barely sleeping — like two, three hours and then right back up, already thinking about the shop and what I was going to do — that’s when the voice was there a lot. I’d be at work, moving fast, making plans in my head, thinking I could reorganize things or get ahead on everything, and I’d hear it through the vents. It felt like it was coming from the vent system, not like just a thought.

And during that same time I was also really sure the chargers and cameras were being used to watch me. Like I’d look at them and it felt connected, like they weren’t just regular equipment sitting there. So yes, when I was sleeping that little and running around with all these big plans, the voice and the feeling of being watched were both going on.
Has there been a time when you were hearing the voice even though your mood felt normal?

Yes… there were times like that too.

It’s hard for me to separate it cleanly, because when things are really intense everything kind of overlaps, but yes — there were a few quieter weeks where I wasn’t in that sped-up mode. I was sleeping more, not just two or three hours, and I wasn’t waking up with all these huge plans like I had to fix everything or reorganize the whole garage or whatever.

My mood felt more… regular, I guess. Not amazing, not terrible, just more like myself. But the voice didn’t completely go away. I would still hear it at the garage, like coming from that same area, the vents or the building somehow. And even though I wasn’t feeling all revved up, I still had that feeling that my husband and my boss were tracking me or watching what I was doing.

That’s part of what makes it hard to explain, because I can’t just say it only happened when my mood was really up. Even when I was more calm and sleeping more normally, it was still there.
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I’ve had bad days, and I’ve had times where I felt worn down or discouraged, but I don’t know if I’d say there was a solid two weeks where I was depressed most of the day nearly every day.

When you say depressed, do you mean like crying and can’t get out of bed, or just feeling low and heavy? Because I can get overwhelmed, but it’s hard for me to separate that from being stressed or exhausted. I don’t want to say yes if it wasn’t really that. I just… I’m not sure I’ve noticed a period like that in the way you’re describing.
Did there ever come a time when that unusually high-energy, little-sleep state lasted at least a full week?

Yes. Definitely more than a week.

It wasn’t just like one weird weekend or a few nights where I couldn’t sleep. Those stretches with barely any sleep, and me feeling like I had all this energy and all these plans running through my head, they’ve been going on for… I’d say around eleven months now. Not every single second exactly the same, but the pattern has been there for that long.

There were times I’d sleep maybe two or three hours and still get up feeling like I needed to be moving, fixing things, doing more, like I couldn’t slow down. And it would keep going past a week — way past a week. It kind of became normal to me after a while, even though looking back, I guess it wasn’t normal.
Was there ever a time when the voice and the feeling of being tracked lasted for at least two weeks while your mood was not unusually high or unusually depressed?

Yes… I think so. That’s actually what I was trying to explain before, but I know I kind of talk around it.

There were a few weeks where I wasn’t in that really high-energy state. I was sleeping more normally, or at least more than before, and I wasn’t waking up with my head full of giant plans or feeling like I had to do everything right then. I felt quieter, more regular. Not really depressed either, not like I was down all day or anything like that.

But even then, the voice was still there. I’d still hear it around the garage, like it was coming through the building or the vents or somewhere I couldn’t quite pin down. And I still felt like my husband and my boss were tracking me, watching what I was doing somehow. That part didn’t just shut off because my mood calmed down.

So yes, I’d say it did last at least two weeks during a time when my mood wasn’t especially high or especially low.

doctor.question: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: What brought me in is I keep hearing a man’s voice coming from the garage vents and sometimes from under the hood, clear as somebody standing next to me, telling me not to trust my husband or touch certain cars.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I am returning the chief complaint symptom code as instructed.

patient.answer:
Um… yeah, hi. I’m here because I keep hearing this man’s voice, and it’s gotten to where I can’t just ignore it or tell myself it’s nothing.

It happens at work a lot — I’m a mechanic, so I’m in the garage all day — and I’ll hear it coming through the vents, like the air vents in the shop, but not muffled like someone far away. It’s clear, like there’s a man standing right next to me talking into my ear. And sometimes it’s when I’m under the hood of a car, like the voice is coming from inside the engine bay or underneath something, even when nobody is there.

He says things like I shouldn’t trust my husband, or he’ll tell me not to touch certain cars. And I know that sounds… I know how it sounds. But in the moment it feels so real, like I can hear the direction it’s coming from and everything. It’s been scaring me, and it’s messing with me at work because I’ll hesitate before doing something I’ve done a thousand times. That’s really what brought me in.

patient.answer:
It’s been… about ten months now, I think. Not like I can point to the exact day and circle it on a calendar, but around that. Close to a year, but not quite.

At first I kept thinking maybe it was just something in the shop, like a sound carrying weird or somebody talking where I couldn’t see them, so I didn’t really mark it as “this is the start.” But looking back, it’s been going on for about ten months — the voice, and then the feeling that there’s tracking tied into it too. It hasn’t just been a couple weeks or anything. It’s been long enough that I’ve had time to keep noticing the pattern.

inference.note: Ten-month duration makes acute/transient psychosis (F23.9) less likely. Persistent persecutory delusions with prominent third-person/second-person auditory hallucinations still support primary psychotic disorders; substance/medical causes not yet excluded.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms to distinguish schizophrenia from delusional/unspecified psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Over the past ten months, have you become much less interested in being around other people than you used to be?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: There are stretches where I don’t call anyone back, skip the church potlucks I used to help run, and just sit in the house or the bay staring at tools like I can’t make myself care about any of it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reduced interest in being around other people, which directly matches diminished social interest under negative symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it because it makes me sound like I’m just being rude or lazy, but there are stretches where I just don’t want to be around anybody.

Like, I’ll see people calling or texting and I just… don’t call them back. Not because I hate them or anything, I just can’t make myself pick up the phone and do the whole conversation. And church stuff used to be a big thing for me — I used to help with the potlucks, like actually be involved, set things up, make sure people had what they needed. Lately I’ll just skip it. I’ll tell myself I’m tired, or I’ll go next time, but then next time comes and I still don’t go.

And at work it happens too, kind of. I’ll be in the bay and instead of getting moving like I normally would, I’ll just be standing there looking at the tools or the bench, and it’s like I know I should care, I know I should start the next thing, but there’s this blank feeling. Like I can’t get interested in any of it.

So, yeah, I’ve pulled back from people. More than I used to. It’s not every single second, but there are definitely stretches where I just stay in the house or keep to myself and everything feels like too much effort.

I get why you’re asking, because people always jump to “it must be drugs” when someone says they’re hearing something, but I don’t really have a neat answer ready in my head for that. If you mean something specific by “used,” maybe you can tell me exactly what counts, and I can try to answer it more clearly.

patient.answer:
I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I hear you asking specifically methamphetamine, and I’m not trying to dodge it, I just… I’m not sure what counts in the way you’re asking.

Like, I don’t have a clear “yes, this was happening every week” kind of answer sitting in my head. If you mean, was I regularly using meth during this whole ten months, I don’t think that’s how I’d describe it. But if you mean any exposure, any time, even if it was around people or something happened once, then I’d have to think harder because my memory around all of it isn’t organized neatly.

I know that probably sounds evasive. I’m sorry. I just don’t want to say yes or no and then have it be the wrong kind of answer.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern like that.

I mean, I understand what you’re asking — like whether after I stop drinking, then the voice or that tracked feeling kicks up — but I don’t have it mapped out in my head that neatly. When things get bad, I’m usually already stressed and not sleeping right or just trying to get through the day, so I don’t always stop and think, “Okay, did this happen after alcohol or before alcohol?”

So… I can’t honestly say yes to that. I don’t remember sitting there thinking, “Oh, I stopped drinking and now this is worse.” It doesn’t stand out to me that way. If you need me to, I can try to think through specific times, but just answering right now, I don’t know that I’ve noticed that connection.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained period of manic symptoms, which would point away from a primary schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis and toward a mood-related or substance-related cause.
doctor.question: During these ten months, have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

target_item.manifestation: For weeks at a time I’d sleep maybe two or three hours, wake up before dawn with my mind already in the garage, and feel like sleeping more would just waste time.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yes, that did happen. Not just like one bad night of sleep, either. There were stretches where for weeks at a time I’d only sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I’d wake up before dawn already wide awake, like my head was already at the garage before my body was even up.

It didn’t feel like normal insomnia, where you’re exhausted and miserable and just can’t sleep. It was more like… sleeping felt like a waste of time. Like if I stayed in bed, I was losing hours I could be using. I’d be thinking about work, tools, cars, parts, things I wanted to fix or organize, and my mind would already be running before the sun was up.

And at the time I wouldn’t always think, “This is unusual.” I’d kind of tell myself I was just being productive or that I had momentum. But looking back, yeah, it was definitely much less sleep than usual, and I still felt like I had energy to keep going.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the decreased need for sleep and increased energy occurred during the same period as the voice and tracking beliefs, which would support a manic episode with psychotic features over a primary psychotic disorder.

patient.answer:
Yes. Yeah, that was happening then too.

When I was in those stretches where I was barely sleeping — like two, three hours and then right back up, already thinking about the shop and what I was going to do — that’s when the voice was there a lot. I’d be at work, moving fast, making plans in my head, thinking I could reorganize things or get ahead on everything, and I’d hear it through the vents. It felt like it was coming from the vent system, not like just a thought.

And during that same time I was also really sure the chargers and cameras were being used to watch me. Like I’d look at them and it felt connected, like they weren’t just regular equipment sitting there. So yes, when I was sleeping that little and running around with all these big plans, the voice and the feeling of being watched were both going on.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms ever occurred outside of mood episodes, which best distinguishes bipolar disorder with psychotic features from schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis.

patient.answer:
Yes… there were times like that too.

It’s hard for me to separate it cleanly, because when things are really intense everything kind of overlaps, but yes — there were a few quieter weeks where I wasn’t in that sped-up mode. I was sleeping more, not just two or three hours, and I wasn’t waking up with all these huge plans like I had to fix everything or reorganize the whole garage or whatever.

My mood felt more… regular, I guess. Not amazing, not terrible, just more like myself. But the voice didn’t completely go away. I would still hear it at the garage, like coming from that same area, the vents or the building somehow. And even though I wasn’t feeling all revved up, I still had that feeling that my husband and my boss were tracking me or watching what I was doing.

That’s part of what makes it hard to explain, because I can’t just say it only happened when my mood was really up. Even when I was more calm and sleeping more normally, it was still there.

inference.note: Psychosis persists during euthymic periods, making a primary mood disorder less likely though bipolar I with psychotic features remains possible. Delirium and substance/alcohol-induced psychotic disorders are less supported by the current history and are dropped.

When you say depressed, do you mean like crying and can’t get out of bed, or just feeling low and heavy? Because I can get overwhelmed, but it’s hard for me to separate that from being stressed or exhausted. I don’t want to say yes if it wasn’t really that. I just… I’m not sure I’ve noticed a period like that in the way you’re describing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was a period of mania lasting at least one week, which would help distinguish bipolar I disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia or unspecified psychosis.
doctor.question: Did there ever come a time when that unusually high-energy, little-sleep state lasted at least a full week?

target_item.name: Manic Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The long stretches of little sleep, racing plans, and nonstop activity have been happening for around eleven months.

patient.answer:
Yes. Definitely more than a week.

It wasn’t just like one weird weekend or a few nights where I couldn’t sleep. Those stretches with barely any sleep, and me feeling like I had all this energy and all these plans running through my head, they’ve been going on for… I’d say around eleven months now. Not every single second exactly the same, but the pattern has been there for that long.

There were times I’d sleep maybe two or three hours and still get up feeling like I needed to be moving, fixing things, doing more, like I couldn’t slow down. And it would keep going past a week — way past a week. It kind of became normal to me after a while, even though looking back, I guess it wasn’t normal.

inference.note: A clear manic syndrome is supported (≥1 week of decreased need for sleep and increased energy), while psychotic symptoms also occur during euthymic periods, making schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type more likely and keeping bipolar I with psychotic features, schizophrenia, and unspecified psychosis in the differential.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been at least a 2-week period of hallucinations or delusions in the absence of any major mood episode, which would distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think so. That’s actually what I was trying to explain before, but I know I kind of talk around it.

There were a few weeks where I wasn’t in that really high-energy state. I was sleeping more normally, or at least more than before, and I wasn’t waking up with my head full of giant plans or feeling like I had to do everything right then. I felt quieter, more regular. Not really depressed either, not like I was down all day or anything like that.

But even then, the voice was still there. I’d still hear it around the garage, like it was coming through the building or the vents or somewhere I couldn’t quite pin down. And I still felt like my husband and my boss were tracking me, watching what I was doing somehow. That part didn’t just shut off because my mood calmed down.

So yes, I’d say it did last at least two weeks during a time when my mood wasn’t especially high or especially low.
